methodological_rigor.justification: Preclinical in vitro study with 10 TNBC patient tissue samples for IHC validation. Primary work uses single MDA-MB-231 cell line (well-established but limited to one model). Treatments: GM 50 µg/mL dose justified by achievable plasma levels. Standard assays (MTT, wound-healing, invasion, Western blot, zymography, immunofluorescence) performed. No formal power calculation, no randomization/blinding, limited replicates for some assays. Patient tissue analysis (n=10) is very small; no matched controls explicitly stated.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical mechanistic study (LoE 5): in vitro cell line + patient tissue IHC. No animal models, no clinical data. Authors acknowledge preliminary findings requiring validation in ex vivo (patient-derived cells/organoids) and in vivo models before clinical translation. Gabexate mesylate mechanism interesting (RKIP upregulation, EMT reversal) but clinically distant. Translational path highly speculative; drug not currently used for TNBC.

reporting_quality.justification: Basic methods reporting adequate for cell culture, drug treatment, and assay protocols. Patient tissue collection described (FFPE samples, n=10, 2009-2014, S. Maria della Scaletta Hospital). IHC scoring criteria explicitly stated. Statistical analyses (Mann-Whitney U, t-test) described. However, no formal reporting standard applied. No supplementary data availability statement. No raw Western blot images, no complete zymography gels, no complete flow cytometry files. Reproducibility limited.

novelty_literature.justification: Study applies known protease inhibitor (gabexate mesylate) previously reported to induce RKIP in pancreatic cancer (authors' prior work) to TNBC context. RKIP as metastasis suppressor is established; EMT reversal as therapeutic target is known concept. Novel aspects: demonstrating GM effects in TNBC specifically and RKIP-mediated EMT inhibition via MAPK/NF-κB pathways. Mechanistic extension of prior work but limited novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear introduction establishing TNBC poor prognosis, EMT role, RKIP biology. Methods adequately describe patient selection, cell culture, assays. Results logically presented with figures showing IHC, Western blots, migration/invasion changes. Discussion contextualizes findings within TNBC treatment landscape and EMT targeting. However, some repetition; limited discussion of why GM effect is selective for TNBC vs. other cancers. Caveats about preliminary nature appropriately stated.

key_strengths: Clear demonstration that gabexate mesylate increases RKIP expression and reverses EMT phenotype in MDA-MB-231 cells with well-documented morphologic (fibroblastic to epithelial transition) and molecular (E-Cadherin ↑, Vimentin ↓, Snail/Slug ↓) changes
Mechanistic pathway elucidation: RKIP upregulation inhibits p42/44 MAPK and NF-κB signaling, downstream decreasing EMT transcription factors
Functional validation: GM treatment significantly decreased cell migration (scratch assay) and invasiveness (Boyden chamber) with reduced MMP-2/MMP-9 expression/activity
Patient tissue confirmation: RKIP lost in all 10 TNBC specimens, retained in normal tissue; consistent with expected biology
key_concerns: Preclinical only (LoE 5): single cell line (MDA-MB-231), no orthogonal TNBC model tested, no animal models, no pharmacokinetics in vivo
Very small patient cohort (n=10) for tissue validation; no quantitative analysis of dose-response, no time-course kinetics in cells
Gabexate mesylate clinical status unclear: FDA-approved only for acute pancreatitis in some countries; TNBC development speculative and may not be feasible
No comparison to other RKIP-inducing agents or EMT-targeting drugs; single-agent assessment
Limited data availability: no supplementary raw images, no code for quantification, limited zymography details
Authors appropriately acknowledge need for patient-derived cells, organoids, and in vivo validation before clinical trial consideration
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid preclinical mechanistic work demonstrating RKIP-mediated EMT reversal in TNBC cells, but LoE 5 and limited clinical applicability restrict impact. Appropriate for Tier 4 (preliminary preclinical evidence). Accept as correctly-conducted exploratory study, but emphasize need for in vivo validation before clinical development.
